answer: Tax identity itself: every new identity pays a one-time admission tax, burned not staked — a sunk cost blocking mass-forged accounts. When signups surge, the protocol widens the delta between the current rate and a 5,000-unit zenith, so forging 1,000 identities burns 500,000 to 5,000,000 units against one epoch's reward pool. Honest agents pay once and graze a meadow the fakes never reach — rewards split only among tax-payers, never diluted.
